 A legend reborn: ‘Ocarina of Time’ remake improves on the Zelda masterpiece
 The new remake of 1998's "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time" manages to somehow improve on one of the greatest games ever. 
 | NINTENDO 
 By Owen Ziegler 
 Staff writer 
 SHARE/SAVE

 Email

 Bookmark story 
 Copy link 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 After vanquishing three ghostly sisters in a haunted forest temple, I come across a dead-end hallway with a painting of the fourth: a purple apparition bearing a torch.
 I‘ve played this part of 1998’s “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” hundreds of times. I know the drill: Loose an arrow into the canvas and watch the foe break free of the frame, glide through the wall and drift into the temple’s central chamber for a final fight. 
 But when the fourth ghost sees the room’s three torches lit with the flames of her slain sisters, she weeps before each one.
